summary: DAY adversarial pass challenged all 12 active-batch companies using cumulative primary evidence plus fresh SEC events. Eleven remain individually ready_for_chief under red-team treatment; SYM remains blocked only because current insider transaction substance is not yet classified. Concentration, dilution, capital intensity and acquisition effects are retained as explicit risk/falsifier evidence rather than converted into invented bearish conclusions.

materialFindings.challenge: Meta-scale committed demand can create customer concentration, GPU-financing and capex-return fragility; falsifier is weak utilization/returns or financing dependence despite contracted capacity.
Fresh Q2 filing/result event reduces staleness risk but backlog/customer wins can still overstate durable cash economics; falsifier is weak margin/cash conversion despite revenue growth.
Framework/offtake narratives must not be treated as operating revenue; licensing, fuel and project-finance dependence remain structural fragilities but future timing alone is non-gating.

Sept. 1 Rockdale land expansion strengthens site-control optionality while increasing the risk of capital deployed ahead of contracted AI/HPC economics; mining cyclicality and financing dilution remain core falsifiers.

Raised 2026 revenue guidance after SkyWater acquisition is not clean evidence of organic quantum demand. Acquisition accounting/integration and equity-funded expansion can inflate narrative momentum; separate acquired manufacturing revenue from quantum platform traction.

90.5% quarterly customer concentration remains extraordinary. Backlog does not neutralize single-customer dependency. Fresh insider Form 4 existence adds a governance event, but transaction substance must be classified before using it bullishly or bearishly.
AI/custom-silicon design-win enthusiasm can hide customer/design concentration and cyclicality; require cash/customer/geographic evidence to remain visible.
AI optics/datacenter demand may be cyclical and capacity/yield sensitive; debt and customer concentration are failure channels if premium growth normalizes.
Hyperscaler concentration and CPO adoption uncertainty can make optical growth fragile; debt equitization is real dilution even when accounting treatment is non-cash.
Distributor/channel concentration can obscure end-customer dependence; manufacturing/geographic concentration is a supply fragility despite strong cash generation.
Three-customer concentration plus AI infrastructure capital intensity can amplify downside if demand normalizes; current margin strength does not eliminate concentration risk.
Diversification is a strength, but large acquisition funding creates integration/leverage risk; synergy realization must not be assumed before evidence.

contradictions: BTDR physical expansion supports optionality while simultaneously increasing pre-demand capital-at-risk.
IONQ guidance growth is real consolidated guidance but acquisition mix prevents treating it as pure organic quantum validation.
SYM backlog visibility coexists with extreme customer concentration.
unknowns: Future customer diversification for NBIS/SYM/optical names
Future quantum commercial adoption and SkyWater integration
